rationale: Evidence from iteration 9 (score 736.5, best so far): the oval (20/20, 1.86 s, max_error 0.010 m) and s-bend (20/20, steering_oscillation 0.29) both finish reliably. The slalom is still the bottleneck: 1/20 finishes, mean progress 0.67 (up from 0.47 at kd 1.5), and about 1.4 line-loss events per run. Across the kd sweep on the slalom, progress went 0.23 (kd 0.8), 0.42 (kd 1.1), 0.47 (kd 1.5), 0.67 (kd 1.8, with base_speed also cut to 0.95). Earlier geometry and speed changes (wider array, forward sensors, higher kp, lower speed alone) all hurt or did not help, so geometry stays fixed. Steering_oscillation has not risen with kd (oval 0.23, s-bend 0.29, both similar to iteration 8), so there is no sign yet that derivative gain is amplifying noise. Change: kd 1.8 to 2.4, with every other value held (geometry, kp 2.2, ki 0.15, base_speed 0.95, last_direction line loss). Hypothesis H1: slalom failure is still lag at sharp alternations, so further damping pushes slalom progress toward 0.8 or more and gives the first consistent slalom finishes. H2: the oval and s-bend stay stable, since their steering_oscillation has been flat across the kd increases. H3 (risk): at kd 2.4 sensor noise is amplified and steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4 on the s-bend, or the oval loses completions. If that happens, the next step is kd about 2.0, or the speed stays at 0.95 while sensor_size is tested at 0.012. Expected result: slalom progress 0.75 or more with line_loss_events below 1.0, s-bend 18/20 or better, oval completion_time about 1.9 s. Next measurements: slalom progress, completion and line_loss_events; s-bend completion and off-track count; steering_oscillation and max_error on all tracks; noise_robustness to see whether noise is becoming the limit.
